channel_name: Invest Like the Best · Patrick O'Shaughnessy
video_title: Inside the Personal AI Assistant Growing 10% a Day | Instinct Founder
gist: Instinct's founder describes a text/voice/email personal AI assistant, invite-only and free, growing about 10% daily with $0 marketing, over $1B annualized transaction volume (half travel), 40% of users sharing a credit card within three weeks, and a merchant take-rate model, while wrestling with months-long compute lead times and incumbent disruption.

insights.claim: Instinct, an invite-only personal AI assistant, is compounding usage roughly 10-11% day over day with zero marketing spend; it started with about 200 friends and family and accelerated from 1-2% to 10% daily as users spent their five invites.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Extreme word-of-mouth growth for a consumer AI product is rare; scarcity-driven referral is the entire growth channel.
insights.quote: we spent $0 on marketing so far

insights.claim: Scarcity of invites created a social game: users brag about invites left, beg for them, and invites were reportedly selling on eBay for about $300.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Artificial scarcity is functioning as both growth throttle and demand signal, while conserving scarce compute.

insights.claim: The invite-only program is framed as a compute-management tool, not exclusivity: the goal is to avoid waking up with 10x users, 80% of whom cannot get responses.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Growth is gated by compute supply, so gated access is a rational strategy for a compute-constrained consumer AI app.

insights.claim: Founder claims the product design principle was understandability over capability: users should be able to predict what will happen when they ask, and that feel is what drove engagement and viral growth.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Suggests product feel and predictability, not model capability, is the differentiator among near-identical agent products.

insights.claim: Message formatting is engineered for reading patterns: front-load information in the first lines because people read about 80% of the first line and taper off, forming a flag shape.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Small UX details in text-based agents are being treated as a moat and tuned via staged rollouts (founder, team, early access, public).

insights.claim: Trust builds over several weeks: three weeks in, about 40% of users have shared a personal credit card with Instinct, and time to first credit card, password or sensitive info is tracked as a trust proxy.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Behavioral evidence that consumers will hand agents payment credentials quickly, which unlocks transaction-based monetization.

insights.claim: Users who connect at least one piece of sensitive information to Instinct show about 80% retention.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Very high retention for consumer software; depth of integration (credentials, email, cards) is the lock-in mechanism.
insights.quote: 80% retention rate. 80% if you share one piece of information.

insights.claim: Security architecture decouples oversight from the agent: all incoming content passes through firewalls that can block malicious content, and every action or thought is monitored by a separate system that can pause, intercept or approve before execution.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: A watchdog architecture separate from the agent's incentives is emerging as the standard mitigation for prompt injection and hallucinated actions.

insights.claim: An early version of the product lacked firewalls and active monitors and had mistakes; the team rebuilt a systematic system rather than patching, and says adversarial testing makes rarer edge cases over time.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Admits early security gaps; the risk of a major breach at a company holding cards, inboxes and calendars remains the key tail risk.

insights.claim: Watchdog example: a validator catches a hallucinated proper noun generated by a sampling error before a thinking trace is executed as a tool call.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Action-time validation is what makes agents with payment access viable despite model hallucination.

themes.theme: Business model: free product, take rate

insights.claim: Instinct is free to users; the plan is a blanket transaction take rate charged to merchants, like Apple Pay or Amex, in exchange for distribution and demand.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Monetizing via merchant take rate rather than subscription or ads is the core bet and depends on agent distribution power.

insights.claim: Platform transaction volume is already above $1 billion annualized on a very small, invite-only user base, with about 50% of it travel; at 10% daily growth it compounds quickly.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Large GMV with few users implies high spend per user and a travel-heavy mix where OTA commissions are rich.

insights.claim: Take-rate benchmarks cited: payments stack roughly 2-2.5%, Shopify 2-3%, Amazon up to about 10%, Apple in-app 30%, and boutique hotels reportedly willing to pay up to about 30% for delivered bookings; the founder is not targeting 30% but the position on the curve is undecided.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Aims at the OTA/marketplace take-rate band rather than payments-rail basis points, which could be a large economic pool taken from incumbents.

insights.claim: The founder deliberately avoids competing on payment-rail margins, calling the roughly 40 intermediaries in a digital transaction a small slice per party, and targets distribution-level take rates instead.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Suggests agent front-ends may capture value above payments infrastructure rather than displace it.

insights.claim: Free-for-life is stated as a personal goal not a commitment; the founder argues subscription pricing (for example $100 per month) is a local optimum that venture capital is meant to help escape.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Signals willingness to burn capital for scale, raising funding needs and compute-cost sensitivity.

insights.claim: Alignment argument: ad-funded platforms like Google, TikTok, Instagram and Snapchat influence behavior against user interest; an agent smarter than its user with an ad model would be dangerous, so Instinct pursues higher-level user objectives rather than being a pure task accomplisher.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Business-model incentives are the real alignment issue for consumer agents, and a free ad-free agent has to make money from merchants without bias.

insights.claim: Agents can exploit first-come-first-served systems: an agent can check every restaurant reservation system every few seconds, and Instinct is working on reinventing reservations so restaurants can prioritize special occasions over first-come slots.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Reservation and booking marketplaces face disintermediation or a redesign around agent-to-agent matching.

insights.claim: Travel agencies and OTAs are the first incumbent category exposed: a voice note like 'I need to be in New York tonight' books flight, seat, hotel, rides and calendar end to end using stored preferences, with the founder expecting collaboration rather than disruption with agencies.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: OTA aggregation and UI value erodes when an agent handles preferences and checkout; travel is already 50% of platform volume.

insights.claim: Founder's framework for incumbents: split each digital business's revenue into attention-on-app (ads, upsell) versus underlying service delivered. Businesses monetizing transactions gain from zero friction; those relying on attention lose.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: A screen for which consumer internet companies win or lose in an agent world: transaction-driven versus attention-driven.

insights.claim: Counterintuitive claim: removing friction may increase total transaction volume for ride-share and food delivery even if in-app attention falls, because a proactive agent will always line up the car or the usual meal.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Argues agents could be net positive for transaction businesses, undermining the bear case on Uber and DoorDash, though the founder admits not knowing their ad share.

insights.claim: Advice to incumbents is to run scaled A/B experiments exposing 1% of users to agent flows to measure transaction volume and discovery impact instead of going all in, and early partner CEOs are already doing this.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Suggests a pattern for how incumbents will engage with agents: pilots and partnerships before conflict.

insights.claim: Founder predicts the internet will be rewritten in coming years, and that most software collapses into one easy interface, reducing consumer app fatigue.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Long-horizon thesis that agent front-ends will aggregate app usage and displace app-store-style distribution.
insights.quote: I think that all of software is going to collapse down into into um honestly a single very very easy to use interface.

insights.claim: Instinct is not tied to iMessage: more than 50% of traffic is not on iMessage, and it will shape-shift across whatever channels users trust, downplaying platform-dependency risk from WhatsApp or Apple.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Distribution rides on Apple and Meta channels that could restrict it; the founder plays this down.

insights.claim: Instinct launched a trusted person network about 10 days before the interview: users connect only to trusted people with per-person access levels (for example spouses share everything, colleagues only work calendar) so agents can negotiate meeting times directly.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: A weighted trust graph among agents is a potential network effect and lock-in beyond single-user utility.

insights.claim: Trust violations propagate socially: if a contact digs for data beyond their granted access, the owner's agent alerts them and the relationship is affected, using social norms as a control layer alongside technical limits.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Novel governance approach to agent privacy; untested at scale.

insights.claim: Users are inventing coordination use cases such as a six-person friend group with weekly agent-planned activities and one Uber optimally routed to pick everyone up.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Illustrates emergent multi-user demand that raises engagement and transaction volume.

insights.claim: Consumer uses include wardrobe scanning with virtual try-on and shopping, and automatically canceling unused subscriptions end to end; the founder says any product dependent on consumer laziness or inertia is toast.
insights.speaker: host, Patrick O'Shaughnessy
insights.so_what: Subscription and consumer inertia revenue (churn-dependent businesses) is directly threatened by agents that audit and cancel.
insights.quote: any product that's dependent on consumer laziness or inertia is toast, huh?

insights.claim: The founder spends about 40% of his time on compute: with usage growing about 10% daily (doubling weekly), buying 2x is consumed in a week, and compute has a lead time of several months, so buying wrong costs a 3-4x tax.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Hyper-growth consumer agents create a compute procurement problem unlike prior apps, favoring holders of contracted capacity.

insights.claim: Even at a slower 5-8% daily compounding over the 3-4 month compute lead time, Instinct would reach roughly 100 million users, forcing a bet on capacity before demand is proven.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale of forward compute commitments a viral agent must make.

insights.claim: Instinct claims to match Opus 5-level frontier performance (engagement, A/B and internal evals) at very low serving cost by shaping inference deployments, since much agent work is batch and needs minutes to hours not milliseconds, allowing 3-8x more efficient deployment shapes.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Latency-tolerant background work lets an agent app cut inference cost sharply versus paying frontier API rates.

insights.claim: Agent workloads are natively proactive: the agent wakes and sleeps on its own (for example scanning at 6am), so token consumption per user is orders of magnitude above interactive coding tools.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Supports the thesis that always-on personal agents drive far more compute demand than codegen, bullish for compute suppliers.
insights.quote: orders of magnitude more than what we than what we thought that we needed

insights.claim: Instinct is growing faster than Claude Code or Codex did, and the founder says this is the most exciting software race ever with trillions of dollars at stake against far larger incumbents with billion-user distribution.
insights.speaker: host, Patrick O'Shaughnessy
insights.so_what: Frames the central risk: viral growth without distribution against incumbents that can distribute to billions immediately.

insights.claim: A subset of users interact almost entirely by voice, with more than 90% of their messages sent by voice, and the founder expects a future of always-on earbuds with an agent triaging contracts, news and calendar.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Voice-first, screenless interaction is a distribution vector for agents, relevant to earbud and phone-OS platforms.

insights.claim: Instinct can generate whole web applications on the fly through a files feature (trip itineraries, wedding plans), replacing the months-long build-ship-feedback cycle of app development.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Generative bespoke interfaces threaten single-purpose apps and long software development cycles.

insights.claim: Interaction will shift from individual tasks to higher-level objectives pursued over months, and the founder sees small businesses whose entire back office, including inventory targets, runs autonomously on Instinct.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Agent-run small business back offices imply demand displacement for SaaS point solutions.

insights.claim: Latest round is reported at about $1 billion at roughly a $10 billion valuation, led by Zoya, Benchmark and Kotu; the founder says the business is capital intensive and uses venture money to prove transaction volume rather than adopt a subscription.
insights.speaker: host, Patrick O'Shaughnessy
insights.so_what: Valuation and backers indicate how investors are pricing consumer agents; funding host-stated and unverified beyond the transcript.

insights.claim: On competitors like Muse, the founder says he spends very little time on competition because few people in a cafe actually use AI the way they imagine, calling the space still open.
insights.speaker: guest, Instinct founder
insights.so_what: Founder sees a large untapped market but has no visible moat beyond product feel and current growth.
